findings.title: Asterisk inside a backtick span, nested in italics, corrupts a whole paragraph of rendered prose
locations: docs/build/architecture.html (rendered D6 'Dominated' alternatives list): rendered text reads `Personal-scope symlinked skills `~/.claude/skills/gbg-*: deliver the checkout's protocol...gbg-prefix costs every/check-docsreference...`
docs/src/architecture.md:383 — source: `*Personal-scope symlinked skills \`~/.claude/skills/gbg-*\`*: deliver the checkout's`
findings.description: The source wraps an alternative's name in italics (*...*) and the name itself contains a code span holding a literal glob asterisk: `~/.claude/skills/gbg-*`. The trailing `*` sits immediately before the closing backtick, so the renderer's emphasis pass closes the italic there instead of at the intended `*` after the backtick, and the backtick that should open a code span is swallowed. The mis-parse cascades: on the built page it corrupts not just that phrase but the following ~90 words spanning four more 'Dominated' alternatives (Plugin skills, Rendered protocol text, Model reads `<root>/PROTOCOL.md`), which come out with code/emphasis tags in the wrong places and a stray literal backtick left in the visible text. Exactly the class RULE.TEX.RENDERED_MARKUP exists to catch — visible only in the built HTML, not the source — verified directly against the built page.
findings.resolution_hint: Drop the trailing `*` from inside the backticks (state the glob wildcard in prose instead) or move the italics outside the code span boundary; rebuild and confirm the cascade clears.

findings.title: Underscores straddling a code-span boundary break a scans-table cell
locations: docs/build/architecture.html (scans table, SCAN.HTML_PUBLIC_HOME row): rendered as `builthtml + \`.gbg/scratch/publicsurface.json\``
findings.description: The bare `built_html` (no backticks) and the code-spanned `.gbg/scratch/public_surface.json` each contain an underscore; the renderer pairs the two underscores as one emphasis span across the intervening code-span boundary, so the built page shows 'built' in roman, then italic 'html + `.gbg/scratch/public', then roman 'surface.json`' with a dangling literal backtick — the surface column of this row is unreadable rather than the intended `built_html + .gbg/scratch/public_surface.json`. Same defect class as the D6 finding above.
findings.resolution_hint: Wrap `built_html` in backticks too so no bare underscore is left outside a code span to pair across the boundary; rebuild and confirm the cell renders as plain text.

findings.title: A bare rule id with an underscore renders with a spurious italic mid-word
locations: docs/build/guide/rules.html (Declared deviations, RULE.API.POSITIONAL entry): rendered as `...is a KNOWN WEAKNESS by RULE.TEST.RULEWITHCHECK's own terms...`
docs/src/guide/rules.md:641 — source: `...is a KNOWN WEAKNESS by RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK's own terms, carried by review...` (the only rule id among the five deviation bullets not backticked)
findings.description: Every other rule id in this deviations list is backticked (RULE.TEST.ALLOC_ZERO, RULE.TEST.PASS_AUDIT, RULE.TEST.EXAMPLES_RUN, RULE.DOC.LEADING_IDENTITY, RULE.API.POSITIONAL); RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK is the sole bare mention, and its underscores are read as emphasis markers, italicising 'WITH' in the rendered word — a direct violation of the FORMATTED rule that every code identifier is backticked, never bare, visible only on the built page.
findings.resolution_hint: Backtick the id: `RULE.TEST.RULE_WITH_CHECK`, matching the other four ids in the same bullet list.

findings.title: Config.check_paths docstring omits two of the checks its own code runs
locations: docs/build/api/Config.html (Config.check_paths): enumerates surface-glob, anchor, module, [paths], extensions/docs_build/executable_claims/seed_catalog checks only
src/CLI/Config.jl:199-200 — glossary-file-exists check and built_html-implies-docs/-directory check, neither named in the docstring
findings.description: check_paths (rendered on the built API page) runs two more existence checks the docstring's enumeration never names: the optional surfaces.glossary file's existence, and that a docs/ directory exists whenever surfaces.built_html is set. Per RULE.DOC.CURRENT a summary naming only a subset of what the code now checks is stale even though every listed item is itself true.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the glossary and built_html/docs-directory checks to the docstring's enumeration in src/CLI/Config.jl.
